::: {#sol-log-loss-curve}

::: {#fig-log-loss-curve}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A smooth U-shaped curve of mean log loss against cutoff, from 0 to 16.
#|   It is high at both ends, falls steadily to a single lowest point
#|   at a middle cutoff, and rises steadily after it.
def mean_log_loss(c):
    """Mean log loss of the soft 0-or-1 rule with cutoff `c`."""
    p = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(ink_01 - c)))
    return -np.mean(np.where(is_one, np.log(p), np.log(1 - p)))

log_loss = np.array([mean_log_loss(c) for c in cutoffs])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(cutoffs, log_loss)
ax.set_xlabel(r"cutoff $\theta$ on center ink")
ax.set_ylabel("mean log loss")
plt.show()
```

The mean [log loss](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/logistic-regression.html#def-log-loss) of the soft 0-or-1 rule among the images of 0s and 1s,
against the cutoff.
